# CDN

*Concept* · also written CDNs · content delivery network · content delivery networks

A content delivery network: servers in front of a site that cache and deliver its pages and files, whose bot protection, firewall rules or throttling can block or slow Google's crawlers.

Narrative: the topic [Crawl errors](../topics/crawl-errors.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

18 claims mention it: 2 from Google's documentation, 9 shown or said at the event (2 not in Google docs, 1 confirmed by Google docs, 6 consistent with Google docs), 7 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [Crawling December: CDNs and crawling](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2024/12/crawling-december-cdns).

- [`D2-C376`](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) Docs: Google's Search Central post on CDNs says that if Google cannot recognise an error message served with a 200 status as an error, all pages showing the same message may be dropped from the index as duplicates, and recovery can be slow because Google has little incentive to recrawl duplicates. For bot-verification interstitials it recommends sending crawlers a 503 status. `[D2-C376, docs, Search Central blog (24 December 2024), https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2024/12/crawling-december-cdns]`
- [`D2-C593`](../sessions/D2-S15-focusing-on-internationalisation-and-localisation.md) Docs: Google's documentation calls a ccTLD a strong signal that a site is meant for a certain country and still lists server location as a possible signal of a site's audience, though not a definitive one because sites use CDNs or are hosted abroad; it does not rank the signals. `[D2-C593, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/specialty/international/managing-multi-regional-sites]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D1-C529`](../sessions/D1-S07-how-google-interprets-robots-txt.md) Stage, Day 1, not in Google docs: Google said the robots.txt report helps catch CDNs that update a site's robots.txt without the owner's knowledge, and hosts that cloak the robots.txt file, which happens more often than people think. `[D1-C529, stage, Google, Day 1]`
- [`D2-C920`](../sessions/D2-S13-using-images-to-your-advantage-and-engaging-search-users-with-videos.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: Serving videos from a content delivery network (CDN) that loads them faster than the site's own server is a win for video SEO, Gary Illyes said. `[D2-C920, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 2]`
- [`D1-C376`](../sessions/D1-S10-how-google-thinks-about-crawl-budget.md) Stage, Day 1, confirmed by Google docs: Hostload applies per host, not necessarily per site: depending on how a site is configured, its CDN, its app, its subdomains and its main www host may be different hosts. `[D1-C376, stage, Google, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C360`](../sessions/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) Stage, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: When Search Console reports network errors, the first step Google recommends is to ask the hosting provider, or the CDN, whether they changed anything. `[D1-C360, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C361`](../sessions/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) Stage, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: Network timeouts are usually caused close to the site, very often by a firewall, a CDN, the hosting provider or the DNS provider, and Google has no visibility into them. `[D1-C361, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C363`](../sessions/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) Stage, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: For DNS and network errors caused by a firewall or CDN, Google advises checking whether new firewall rules were set recently and otherwise asking in the CDN's forum, as Google itself cannot see or help with these errors. `[D1-C363, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C364`](../sessions/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) Stage, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: A rise in HTTP errors in crawl reports can come from a CDN throttling crawlers by injecting 429 or 503 responses on the network path between Google's crawler and the site. `[D1-C364, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C367`](../sessions/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) Stage, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: CDN captcha challenges often return HTTP 200; Googlebot does not solve them and sees only content with a 200 status, which indexing then classifies as a soft 404, reported as an error in Search Console. `[D1-C367, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 1]`
- [`D2-C374`](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: A growing cause of wrong clustering is bot protection: when a CDN or another protection system shows Googlebot the same 'you look like a bot, solve this puzzle' page on many unrelated URLs or domains, Google can cluster those pages as duplicates. `[D2-C374, stage, Google, Day 2]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D1-C371`](../sessions/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) Analysis: Day 1 said a CDN captcha page served with HTTP 200 becomes a soft 404, while Day 2 (D2-C374, D2-C375) said such challenge pages are hard to recognise as errors and can be clustered as duplicates; Google's CDN post describes both outcomes, and in both the real pages drop out of Search. `[D1-C371, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D1-C088`](../sessions/D1-S07-how-google-interprets-robots-txt.md) Analysis: Content-Signal lines are now common because a large CDN provider adds them to its managed robots.txt files. Never place any non-standard directive between user-agent lines; put it after a group's rules and test the file with each search engine's tools, such as Bing's robots.txt tester and Google's open-source robots.txt parser. `[D1-C088, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D1-C077`](../sessions/D1-S00-day-1-session-not-recorded.md) Analysis: This does not mean avoiding HTTP/3, which benefits browsers. The rule is never to run a host that only answers over HTTP/3, and to check that CDN or firewall rules written for HTTP/3 traffic do not break HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2. `[D1-C077, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C105`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Analysis: Set max-snippet:-1 and max-image-preview:large on every indexable template unless licensing requires otherwise, and check that no CMS, plug-in or CDN setting adds lower snippet or image preview limits by default. `[D2-C105, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C210`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Analysis: An API or CDN on its own host needs its own robots.txt check: a blanket Disallow there, or a robots.txt that returns 5xx errors, can stop Google fetching the data a page renders from. `[D2-C210, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C298`](../sessions/D2-S06-what-is-google-friendly-javascript.md) Analysis: Check robots.txt for Disallow rules covering JavaScript bundles, build folders or API endpoints the page calls while rendering, including on separate API or CDN hostnames with their own robots.txt, then confirm in URL Inspection's live test that the rendered HTML contains the main content. `[D2-C298, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C378`](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) Analysis: Check what your CDN or bot protection serves to verified Googlebot and to the AI agents you want to allow; if crawlers must get a challenge page, return it with a 503 status as Google recommends, never as a 200 page across many URLs, which Google may cluster as duplicates. `[D2-C378, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`

## For developers

- `DEV-PRF-01` **SHOULD** · Documented: Keep connect time and time to first byte low and stable under crawler load (1 of its claims mentions it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-SRV-01` **MUST** · Documented: Let verified Google crawlers through firewalls, CDNs and bot protection (4 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-SRV-02` **AVOID** · Documented: Never serve bot challenges or error pages to crawlers with a 200 status (5 of its claims mention it)
- `DEV-SRV-04` **MUST** · Documented: Keep robots.txt reachable on every host: 200 with rules, or 404 if there are none (1 of its claims mentions it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-SRV-06` **AVOID** · Documented: Do not put Content-Signal or other non-standard lines between user-agent lines (2 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-VID-06` **SHOULD** · Documented: Serve videos fast in a common container with standard codecs, and never block the files (1 of its claims mentions it; its own text names it)
